items.d: 도널드 트럼프 미국 행정부가 한국, 중국, 일본, 유럽연합(EU) 등을 대상으로 ‘과잉 생산’ 관련 무역법 301조 관세 부과를 25일 발표했다. 집권 공화당의 11·3 중간선거 참패와 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)와 관련된 대중 수출통제 위반 논란으로 궁지에 몰린 트럼프 행정부가 다시 보복 관세에 시동을 걸고 있다.  미 무역법 301조는 행정부가 자국 기업에 차별적인 외국 정부의 정책이나 관행에 대해 무역 보복 조치를 할 수 있게 한 조항이다. 트럼프 행정부는 2월 연방대법원에서 무효가 된 상호관세를 대신할 관세 보복 수단으로 무역법 301조를 동원했다. 7월 한국에 대해 무역법 301조를 근거로 ‘강제 노동’ 관세 12.5%를 부과한 데 이어 이번에 ‘과잉 생산’ 관세가 새로 부과된 것이다.

items.fullText: 핫픽! 미국주식 핫픽! 미국주식 엔비디아 시간외 6% 급락…美 물가·관세 충격에 AI株 휘청 [월가 업&다운] 입력 2026.11.25 23:17 수정 2026.11.25 23:23 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 황정수 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. AI 기사요약 미국 물가 상승세 재점화와 백악관의 신규 관세 부과 방침으로 엔비디아를 비롯한 AI 관련주와 뉴욕증시 선물이 급락한 가운데, 추가 금리 인상 우려와 AI 투자 수익성에 대한 의구심이 시장의 변수로 부각되고 있습니다. 10월 PCE 물가 3.8% 상승 추가 금리 인상 우려 나스닥 선물 3% 하락 헬스케어·필수소비재 등 방어주로 자금 이동 월스트리트 표지판 /사진=REUTERS 미국의 물가 상승세가 다시 확대되고 백악관이 신규 관세 부과 방침을 발표하면서 엔비디아를 비롯한 인공지능(AI) 관련주와 뉴욕증시 주요 지수 선물이 급락했다. 추가 금리 인상 가능성이 커지는 가운데 AI 인프라 투자 비용과 수익성에 대한 우려까지 겹치면서 투자자들의 위험자산 회피 심리가 확산하는 모습이다. 나스닥 선물 3% 하락 25일(현지시간) 미국 경제매체 CNBC에 따르면 이날 오전 9시 기준 나스닥100 지수 선물은 3% 급락했다. 다우존스30 산업평균지수 선물은 635포인트(1.3%), 스탠더드앤드푸어스(S&P)500 지수 선물은 2% 각각 하락했다. AI 관련 기업들이 하락세를 주도했다. 엔비디아는 개장 전 거래에서 6% 하락했고 앤트로픽과 알파벳은 각각 4%, 오라클은 약 6% 떨어졌다. 스테이트스트리트의 기술주 상장지수펀드(ETF)인 테크놀로지 셀렉트 섹터 ETF(XLK)도 3% 넘게 하락했다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. AI 포인트 뷰 이전 분석 종목 다음 분석 종목 본 서비스의 AI가 제공하는 종목 정보는 정보 제공 목적의 참고 자료일 뿐, 투자 권유·자문·추천에 해당하지 않습니다. 투자에 따른 손실 책임은 사용자에게 있습니다. 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 황정수 특파원 안녕하세요. 국제부 뉴욕특파원입니다. 관련 뉴스

items.d: Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., discusses Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer and his value to the AI growth cycle and overall market. SK하이닉스 도 11% 넘게 떨어졌다. 한국거래소에 따르면 이날 코스피지수는 전 거래일보다 308.52포인트(6.16%) 떨어진 4697.51을 기록했다. 전날 상승분을 거의 반납한 것이다. 코스피지수 급락에 장 초반 매도 사이드카(프로그램매도 호가 일시 효력 정지)가 발동하기도 했다. 삼성전자 보통주는 1만8700원(9.87%) 내린 17만700원에 정규장 거래를 마쳐 시가총액이 약 997조9600억원으로 내려앉았다. 삼성전자 보통주 시가총액이 1000조원을 밑돈 것은 지난 3월31일 이후 처음이다. 다만 보통주와 우선주를 합산한 삼성전자 전체 시가총액은 여전히 1000조원을 넘는다. SK하이닉스는 12만8000원(11.05%) 떨어진 103만원에 정규장 거래를 마쳤다. 이에 따라 삼성전자 단일종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF)는 20% 가까이 하락했다. 삼성자산운용의 ' KODEX 삼성전자단일종목레버리지 '는 전 거래일 대비 19.10% 내린 4680원에, ' TIGER 삼성전자단일종목레버리지 '는 19.54% 떨어진 4220원에 마감했다. 이 밖에 ' RISE 삼성전자단일종목레버리지 '(-19.35%), ' PLUS 삼성전자단일종목레버리지 '(-19.32%), ' ACE 삼성전자단일종목레버리지 '(-19.21%), ' 1Q 삼성전자선물단일종목레버리지 '(-18.94%), ' KIWOOM 삼성전자선물단일종목레버리지 '(-18.93%) 등도 줄줄이 하락해 신저가를 새로 썼다. SK하이닉스 단일종목 레버리지도 상황이 비슷하다. 삼성자산운용의 ' KODEX SK하이닉스단일종목레버리지 '는 21.72% 내린 3135원에, 미래에셋자산운용의 ' TIGER SK하이닉스단일종목레버리지 '는 21.70% 떨어진 2670원에 마감했다. items.t: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy
items.d: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting The CEO acknowledged that he had gone ‘too far’ with some of his workplace behavior and said he has been going to therapy every day, a source told NBC News. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tech stocks take a dip as Jensen Huang comes back as Nvidia CEO 04:53 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 11:11 PM EST By Jean Lee and Jared Perlo Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world. According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source. Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. items.t: Trump says pardon is always an option for Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary
items.d: The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has sparked bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week.
items.fullText: Donald Trump Trump says pardon is always an option for Jensen Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has drawn skepticism on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 President Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 9:19 PM EST By Kyla Guilfoil President Donald Trump said that while pardoning Jensen Huang for any potential criminal activity remains an option, he doesn’t think that will be needed for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO . “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview published Tuesday night. Asked about Huang’s scheduled appearances next week on Capitol Hill, Trump said, “I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people.” “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said. A representative for Huang declined to comment on Trump’s comments. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for further comment. Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated he would have told Trump if Huang had been involved in any criminal activity. “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. items.t: Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on probe
items.d: Attorney General Todd Blanche praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang.
items.fullText: Trump administration Todd Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on investigation President Donald Trump had said the Justice Department had “exonerated” the chip giant’s newly reinstated CEO, Jensen Huang. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Blanche says he would have told Trump about any crimes Jensen Huang committed 01:22 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 1:37 PM EST By Dareh Gregorian and Helen Graham Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he’d spoken to Blanche and “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated,” referring to Huang. Asked at an unrelated press conference about Trump’s remarks, Blanche said, “What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him,” before adding, “I’m not going to get into communications I have with the president about it.” He then said that what Trump was saying “is exactly right.” “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. NBC News previously reported that Trump sought Blanche and Vice President JD Vance’s help in convincing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. An administration official said the attorney general told the president that the DOJ had no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang or the company. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w
